chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Usman ibn Isa, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic
Thus will Allah show them their deeds to be intense regret to them

He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the man who leaves his wealth and does not spend it in obedience to Allah out of stinginess, then he dies leaving it for the one who works with it in obedience to Allah or in disobedience to Allah. So if he works with it in obedience to Allah, he sees it in the Scale of someone else, so he experiences regret, and the wealth was once his; but if he works with it in disobedience to Allah, that wealth enables him (the spender) to disobey Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.حَسَرَاتٍ: Regret or intense sorrow over lost opportunity

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'regret' in the verse 'Thus will Allah show them their deeds to be intense regret to them'?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi offers a nuanced exegesis of Quran 2:167, illustrating how unspent wealth becomes a source of spiritual regret (hasrah) for the stingy owner, whose 'scale' reflects the deeds performed by heirs using that wealth. It highlights the Shia concept of the continuity of spiritual accounting, where the original owner's share in the outcome depends on whether the heir utilizes the funds for obedience or disobedience. This underscores the practical imperative of active expenditure (infaq) rather than mere accumulation.
